title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Cases by Circuit Courts

articles.content_en:
Article 1 The Supreme People's Court shall establish circuit courts to accept relevant cases within the circuit areas. The First Circuit Court shall be located in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, and its circuit area shall include Guangdong, Guangxi, and Hainan provinces. The Second Circuit Court shall be located in Shenyang, Liaoning Province, and its circuit area shall include Liaoning, Jilin, and Heilongjiang provinces.
The Supreme People's Court may, in accordance with relevant provisions and the needs of adjudication work, establish additional circuit courts and adjust the circuit areas and case acceptance scope of circuit courts.

Article 2 A circuit court shall be a standing adjudicative body dispatched by the Supreme People's Court. Judgments, rulings, and decisions made by a circuit court shall be judgments, rulings, and decisions of the Supreme People's Court.

Article 4 Cases concerning intellectual property, foreign-related commercial matters, maritime and admiralty, death penalty review, state compensation, enforcement, and cases protested by the Supreme People's Procuratorate shall be temporarily adjudicated or handled by the headquarters of the Supreme People's Court.

Article 5 A circuit court shall establish a litigation service center to accept and register case materials falling within the scope of the circuit court's acceptance, and provide litigation services for the parties. Where a party requests that the circuit court transfer materials of cases that shall be accepted by the Supreme People's Court headquarters in accordance with these Provisions, the circuit court shall transfer them.
A circuit court shall, for cases meeting the conditions for filing, uniformly number and file them on the Supreme People's Court case handling information platform.

Article 6 Where a party appeals against a first-instance administrative or civil and commercial judgment or ruling made by a Higher People's Court within the circuit area, the appeal petition shall be submitted to the circuit court through the original trial People's Court. If a party directly appeals to the circuit court, the circuit court shall transfer the appeal petition to the original trial People's Court within five days. Upon receipt of the appeal petition and reply, the original trial People's Court shall, within five days, submit them together with all case files and evidence to the circuit court.

Article 7 Where a party applies for retrial or petitions against an effective judgment or ruling made by a Higher People's Court within the circuit area, the party shall submit materials such as the retrial application or petition to the circuit court.

Article 8 Where the Supreme People's Court considers that a case accepted by a circuit court has significant guiding significance for the uniform application of law, it may decide to have the headquarters adjudicate the case.
Where a circuit court considers that an accepted case has significant guiding significance for the uniform application of law, it may report the case to the Supreme People's Court headquarters for adjudication.
Article 9 A circuit court may, in accordance with the needs of adjudication work, conduct circuit trial of cases and receive visitors within the circuit area.

Article 10 A circuit court shall, in accordance with the principle of letting the adjudicator adjudicate and the adjudicator bears responsibility, implement the responsibility system for presiding judges and collegiate bench case handling. The presiding judges of a circuit court shall be selected by the Supreme People's Court from among adjudication personnel with outstanding case handling ability and rich trial experience. The collegiate bench of a circuit court shall be composed of presiding judges.

Article 11 The chief judge and deputy chief judges of a circuit court shall participate in the collegiate bench to adjudicate cases. When a collegiate bench adjudicates a case, the presiding judge in charge of the case shall serve as the presiding judge. When the chief judge or a deputy chief judge participates in the collegiate bench to adjudicate a case, such person shall serve as the presiding judge. Judgments and rulings made by a circuit court shall be signed by the members of the collegiate bench and issued by the presiding judge.

Article 12 Cases accepted by a circuit court shall be uniformly incorporated into the Supreme People's Court's comprehensive management platform for adjudication information for management, and case filing information, adjudication procedures, and adjudicative documents shall be disclosed to the parties and the public according to law.

Article 13 A circuit court shall have an integrity supervision officer responsible for the daily integrity supervision work of the circuit court.
The Supervision Bureau of the Supreme People's Court shall conduct integrity supervision over circuit courts and their staff by accepting reports and complaints, investigating disciplinary cases, and carrying out judicial inspections and trial supervision.
